findings.summary: Shell command injection: changed from list-based exec_run(['python3', '-c', code]) to string-based exec_run(f'python3 -c "{code}"') — double quotes in Python code escape shell quoting, breaking syntax for any code using string literals and enabling injection of arbitrary shell commands inside the Docker container
findings.failure_scenario: code = 'print("hello world")' produces the shell command python3 -c "print("hello world")" which has unmatched quotes — shell syntax error. Worse, code containing '"; malicious_cmd; echo "' executes arbitrary commands inside the container.

findings.summary: AttributeError: uses datetime.now() on the datetime module (imported via 'import datetime') but now() is a classmethod on datetime.datetime — will raise AttributeError: module 'datetime' has no attribute 'now'
findings.failure_scenario: Any call to _save_results_to_file() (when save_file=True) crashes with AttributeError. The old code correctly used datetime.datetime.now().

findings.summary: Missing raise_for_status() — HTTP errors (4xx, 5xx) are not detected; response.json() is called on error responses, which may not contain valid JSON or may contain an error dict that silently falls through logic
findings.failure_scenario: Serper API returns 401 Unauthorized — response.json() returns {'error': 'Unauthorized'}, code checks 'if "organic" in results' (false), falls to 'else: return results', returning the error dict to the caller who expects search results.

findings.summary: Missing timeout parameter on requests.request() — network calls may hang indefinitely; old code had timeout=10
findings.failure_scenario: Serper API becomes unresponsive — request blocks forever with no timeout, hanging the calling agent indefinitely.

findings.summary: Bare os.environ['SERPER_API_KEY'] access raises unhelpful KeyError without a descriptive error message if the environment variable is not set
findings.failure_scenario: User deploys without setting SERPER_API_KEY environment variable — uncaught KeyError crashes with cryptic traceback instead of clear 'Missing API key' message.

findings.summary: Inconsistent return type: returns formatted string when organic results exist but raw dict otherwise — callers cannot rely on the type of _run()'s return value
findings.failure_scenario: Search yields no organic results (empty results page) — code falls to 'else: return results' returning a raw dict, while callers expecting the formatted search string get a dict and may crash when calling string methods on it.

findings.summary: Command injection in library installation: changed from exec_run(['pip', 'install', library]) to exec_run(f'pip install {library}') — shell metacharacters in library names (from agent/LLM input) allow command injection inside the Docker container
findings.failure_scenario: LLM generates or adversary provides library name containing shell metacharacters like 'requests; cat /etc/passwd; echo' — shell executes pip install requests; cat /etc/passwd; echo inside the container, leaking sensitive data.

findings.summary: Removed URL validation (_validate_url method deleted) — URLs are passed to Spider API without any format or security checks, including javascript: and data: scheme URLs
findings.failure_scenario: URL 'javascript:alert(1)' or 'file:///etc/passwd' is passed unchecked to spider.scrape_url() — Spider client may behave unexpectedly or crash.

findings.summary: Removed all error handling (try/except for ValueError, ImportError, ConnectionError, Exception) — errors during spider operations now propagate uncaught with no graceful message
findings.failure_scenario: Network timeout during spider.scrape_url() — ConnectionError propagates to crewAI framework with no user-friendly error message, potentially crashing the entire agent workflow.

findings.summary: return_format unconditionally overwritten to 'markdown' regardless of user-specified params — users cannot request other formats (text, html, raw) even though the README documents them as supported
findings.failure_scenario: User passes params={'return_format': 'text'} — code at line 53 silently overwrites to 'markdown', producing markdown output instead of expected plain text. Any value in params['return_format'] is discarded.

findings.summary: Removed result_as_answer conditional — _run previously checked self.result_as_answer and returned tool(...).content for callers that wanted text output; now always returns raw ToolOutput object, a silent breaking change
findings.failure_scenario: Existing code with LlamaIndexTool(result_as_answer=True, llama_index_tool=tool) — _run now returns a ToolOutput object instead of a string, and the LLM receives <llama_index.core.tools.types.ToolOutput object at 0x...> instead of the expected text content.

findings.summary: Inconsistent URL validation: schema validator (lines 27-47) checks whitespace, length, and uses urlparse, while _create_driver (lines 131-136) only checks emptiness and scheme prefix — different validation layers enforce different rules depending on whether website_url was preset in __init__
findings.failure_scenario: Tool initialized with website_url preset (args_schema replaced with FixedSeleniumScrapingToolSchema, no validator): URL 'https://example.com ' (trailing space) passes _create_driver but would have been rejected by the schema validator. When used without preset, the schema validator catches it but the _create_driver redundant check does not detect it.

findings.summary: SerpApiGoogleSearchTool and SerpApiGoogleShoppingTool removed from package exports with no deprecation warning — any code importing these symbols gets an immediate ImportError
findings.failure_scenario: Existing code with 'from crewai_tools import SerpApiGoogleSearchTool' — ImportError crashes the application at startup with no migration path.

findings.summary: Removed search_type='news' support and entire news-processing pipeline — users of the news search feature silently fall back to regular web search with no error or warning
findings.failure_scenario: User with search_type='news' in kwargs — the new code ignores search_type entirely, always hitting the /search endpoint. News-specific results are lost and user gets generic web results instead of news articles.

findings.summary: Removed test 'test_run_code_in_docker_with_script' that executed multi-line Python code with quotes — this exact test would have caught the command injection regression at line 111 of code_interpreter_tool.py
findings.failure_scenario: The removed test used multi-line code with print() calls containing double-quoted strings. Under the new f'python3 -c "{code}"' pattern, this test would break with a shell syntax error, immediately flagging the injection vulnerability. Its removal allows the regression to ship undetected.
